tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H26): Three-launch pipeline: custom mma.sync FP16 GEMM1 and GEMM2 with fused epilogues replace cuBLASLt GEMM1+K2 and K3+GEMM2+K4, dispatched per row against the library path. Step 0 (10 min): time the parent and the r0 anchor interleaved x3 under harness_time on all 16 rows in this container and report the clock; these are the controls for every comparison below. Step 0b (10 min, audit H15): cold after the 2xL2 flush, time every cuBLASLt heuristic algo (requestedAlgoCount 32, including split-K configs via the algo attribute) for GEMM1 98/392/784/1568 x 3072 x 768 and GEMM2 98/392/784/1568 x 768 x 3072 in FP16; report the best per shape against bytes/7 TB/s + 2 us. Step 1: build GEMM1f as a per-shape template (M tile 64 or 128, N tile from 64/96/128, K = C): A = d fp16 channel-major as K1 writes it, B = W1 fp16 from K1's conversion, 4-stage cp.async ring with all fragment LDS issued before any HMMA and no runtime guards around HMMA; epilogue z = rstd*(acc - mu*u_k) + v_k + b1 using the parent's LN fold, exact erff, per-(image,k) sum of squares reduced per column in smem then one red.add per tile and column into the 4 accumulator copies, fp16 hidden store with 16-byte stores through an smem-staged rolled loop (B's 48-erff register-direct epilogue took 16 us per tile; the staged loop fixed it). Compare GEMM1f alone against cuBLASLt GEMM1 + K2 at 1,192 (5.1 + 9.8 us) and 8,320 (11 + 37.8 us), interleaved. Step 2: build GEMM2f: prologue sums the 4 sumsq copies for the CTA's image(s), reduces mean_k in-CTA and puts s_k = 1 + gw_k*gf_k/(mean+eps) in smem; A = hidden fp16 scaled by s_k at fragment load; swapped operands (M = C output channels, N = token tile) so each accumulator row is contiguous along hw, giving a coalesced residual x read and NCHW output store and no K4; add b2' = b2 + gb @ W2^T computed by K1's spare CTAs. Compare against K3 + cuBLASLt GEMM2 + K4 at 1,192, 2,768 and 8,384. Step 3: per-row dispatch by interleaved measurement (custom vs library) with the library path kept where it wins (expected 32,128 and 64,96, possibly 8,320 and 32,768 where mma.sync ideal is 29-33 us); the kernel sequence per shape must be fixed. Step 4 (only if steps 1-3 are done): K1 issues cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2 for W1 and W2 at entry (I15) and the hidden stores use evict_last (I11); keep each only if it wins >= 2% interleaved x3 at 2,768 and 8,320. Step 5: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check; log per row the max |err| and the count of elements beyond that row's own atol over the harness's 10 seeded rounds against an fp64 reference; if any row has a beyond-atol element, switch its cheap operand to the hi/lo fp16 split and re-run. Report rented per-row times, the step 0 controls, and the register/spill counts of both GEMM kernels. Success: Interleaved against the parent: 1,192 <= 26 us, 2,768 <= 48, 8,384 <= 60, 8,192 <= 50 rented, no row slower than the parent by more than 2%; run_tests 16/16 with zero beyond-own-atol elements; projected portal >= 0.645. Refuted if: GEMM1f alone at 1,192 is >= 8 us cold (no better than cuBLASLt GEMM1 + K2's chain would allow) or the 3-launch total at 1,192 is >= 30 us rented interleaved; then each custom launch still carries a 6-10 us dependent chain and the lineage's remaining lever is the conv and the C=768 GEMM path only. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s).

Experiment E2 (tests H24): Post-sync round microbench, then rebuild the cooperative kernel's post-sync loads as single bulk copies with every phase-independent operand prefetched at entry. Step 0 (controls): parent and r0 anchor interleaved x3 under harness_time on all 16 rows; report the clock. Step 1 (microbench, the critic's test, 30 min): a cooperative stub with 296 CTAs that does grid.sync then one per-CTA load round of 6 KB, 12 KB and 32 KB as (a) 4-byte cp.async per element with the parent's index maths, (b) 16-byte cp.async or LDG.128 with every load issued before the first wait, (c) one cp.async.bulk plus one mbarrier wait; the source is (i) lines just written by other CTAs before the sync and (ii) cold DRAM after the 2xL2 flush; stamp globaltimer and clock64 per CTA and report median and max round time and B/clk/SM for each of the 18 cells, plus the grid.sync cost alone with and without pending stores before it. Step 2 (branch on step 1): if (c) is <= 1.2 us for 32 KB just-written, rebuild the flat kernel: one producer warp per CTA with mbarrier full/empty pairs issues at kernel entry the CTA's W1 and W2 fp32 slices (converted with cvt.rn.f16x2 at fragment load, so no weight pass at C<=192), all small vectors in one bulk copy, the residual x tile and the conv halo (3-D TMA box starting at w=-4 with box width W+8, taps offset +1 in smem, as A found; 1-D bulk plane copies for W=7/14); after each grid.sync exactly one bulk or tensor copy per operand (the a/hidden tile, gf); epilogues stage in smem and leave through 16-byte or bulk stores; keep the per-shape templates and the shfl-uniform warp index. If (c) is still >= 2 us but (b) is no better, the cost is post-barrier latency: do not rebuild the loads; instead replace sync2 with per-image counters (self-resetting, zeroed in phase 1 of the same call, ld.acquire.gpu spin with nanosleep) and an image-major tile order (H10 / I16) at 8,192,28,28 and 32,768,7,7, and measure that interleaved x3. Step 3: interleaved A/B against the parent x3 on 1,192; 1,96; 1,160; 2,96; 4,192; 4,96; 8,192; 2,768; set the dispatch per row from that. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check and the per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol counts over the harness's 10 seeded rounds; apply the hi/lo split where needed. Report the microbench table in the findings whatever the branch taken. Success: Bulk branch: 1,192 <= 22 us and 2,96 <= 32 us rented interleaved (parent 29.8 / 43.4), the other S rows -6 us or more; projected portal >= 0.60. Dataflow branch: >= 6 us faster per row at 8,192 and 32,768. Refuted if: The 32 KB just-written bulk round after a grid.sync costs >= 2 us in the microbench and the rebuilt kernel (either branch) is within 2 us of the parent at 1,192 and 2,96; then the cooperative kernel's floor is barrier-side latency, H24 is refuted, and B's thesis of S rows <= 20 us needs a barrier-free dataflow or should be retired in r4. This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. Experiment E3 (tests H25): Weight-stationary cooperative kernel for the six wide-C small-image rows: fp32 weights ingested once per call through TMA/bulk rings, whole-image token tiles with CTA-local GRN statistics, bulk-plane conv. Target rows: 2,768,7,7; 8,768,7,7; 16,768,7,7; 32,768,7,7; 8,384,14,14; 16,384,14,14. The other 10 rows route to the r0 baseline paths through a shape dispatch (correct for all 16). Step 0 (controls): r0 anchor x3 interleaved under harness_time on the six rows; report the clock. Step 1 (stub probe, 30 min, kill gate): a cooperative kernel of <= 148 CTAs that, after the 2xL2 flush, issues at entry a bulk/TMA copy of each CTA's real fp32 W1 and W2 slice bytes (distinct slices, 19 MB total at C=768; 4.7 MB at C=384; TFLOAT32 or FLOAT32 maps, or 1-D cp.async.bulk of contiguous rows), copies 4-channel 7x7 plane groups (784 B) or single 14x14 planes (784 B) with 1-D cp.async.bulk into zero-padded smem planes with all copies issued before any store, does two grid syncs each followed by one bulk load of the real a-tile or hidden-tile size, and red.adds the real GEMM2 partial volume into a prefilled output; harness_time at 2,768 and 32,768. Kill the kernel build if the stub exceeds 20 us at 2,768 or 35 us at 32,768 and spend the rest of the session finding which term is responsible (weight ingest vs post-sync rounds vs red.add) with globaltimer stamps. Step 2: tile table per row with T a multiple of HW (tiles hold whole images) and BN a multiple of 16, e.g. 2,768: T=98, BN=24 (128 CTAs); 8,768: T=196, BN=48; 16,768: T=392, BN=64; 32,768: T=392, BN=96 (4 token tiles x 32 slices = 128 CTAs); 8,384: T=196, BN=64; 16,384: T=392, BN=96; adjust to fit smem (fp32 W1 slice BN*C*4 plus W2 slice C*BN*4, through a ring when above ~100 KB; hidden slice T*BN*2 fp16). Phase A per CTA: bulk-plane conv for its channel share, d written fp16 channel-major to L2 plus per-token LN partial sums, output prefilled with x + b2' (b2' = b2 + gb @ W2^T by spare warps), while a producer warp streams the W1 slice (fp32, resident or ring; convert with cvt.rn.f16x2 at fragment load, never inside the ring); all small vectors bulk-loaded at entry. Sync 1. Phase B: GEMM1 over T tokens x BN hidden with K = C using mma.sync m16n8k16 FP16 (per-shape templates, all fragment LDS first, no runtime guards around HMMA); A = d streamed from L2 in k-chunks; LN applied in the epilogue as r*(acc - mu*s1) + c1 (B's fold); exact erff; hidden slice fp16 kept in smem; per-(image,k) sum of squares is CTA-local because tiles hold whole images, so write gf[b][k] directly and one per-image partial sum over the CTA's k (no atomics). Sync 2. Phase C: read the B x (4C/BN) partial sums (one bulk round), form s_k for the CTA's own channels, scale the smem hidden slice, GEMM2 partial with K = BN against the W2 slice streamed during phase B, red.global.add into the prefilled NCHW output (rows contiguous along hw). Per row decide by arithmetic between red.add split-K (volume M*C*4*(4C/BN) at 4.2 TB/s) and materialising the scaled fp16 hidden in L2 followed by a c-sliced GEMM2 (B's path), and state the choice in the findings. Step 3: interleaved x3 against the r0 anchor on the six rows; globaltimer stamps per phase at 2,768 and 32,768. Step 4: run_tests 16/16 with the portal-order check and the per-row max |err| and beyond-own-atol counts over the harness's 10 seeded rounds; apply the hi/lo split where needed. Report the stub table, the tile table, phase stamps and per-row rented times. Success: 2,768 <= 35 us, 8,768 <= 45, 32,768 <= 75 rented (A r2: 64.3 / 63.1 / 97.0; leader-implied 27 / 34 / 67), with 16,768 <= 55 and 8,384 <= 45; run_tests 16/16; the six rows together project >= +0.03 of mean over A r2. Refuted if: The stub in step 1 exceeds 20 us at 2,768 or 35 us at 32,768, or the full kernel is not at least 10 us faster than A r2 at both 2,768 and 8,768 interleaved; then the wide-C rows are bound by post-sync rounds or weight ingest rather than by A's launch chain, and D's thesis moves to a 3-launch TF32 swap-AB specialist (I18) or is retired.
